$comment: v3 REFUSAL VECTORS, SUPPLIED BY CC CORPUS 2026-08-20, copied verbatim.
Two are SERVED RECORDS lifted unmodified from the running corpus on 9093. The third is
CONSTRUCTED, signed with the same refusal key, and named so because nothing on that
WHY THE CONSTRUCTED ONE IS NOT OPTIONAL, and it is the reason this file has three rows and
not two. The recorded arm's note path is UNEXERCISED on the live corpus: 18 of 145 refusals
sit on that arm and none carries a note, because the ceiling refusal builds
{state, limit, unit, observed} and never sets one. Vectors taken only from what the service
serves would exercise the recorded arm WITHOUT its note, and a page could pass both served
records while silently dropping the field v3 exists to sign. Same shape as the served-row
population carrying no nulls, and as every row carrying a digest credential.
ALL THREE VERIFY AND ALL THREE REJECT a one-unit change to spend.amountRaw, so a verifier
that passes them is checking rather than agreeing. That is asserted below, not assumed.
ALL THREE ARE STORE SHAPE. Their names say served because they came off the service's store,
not because they are /v1/refusals projections. So served-shape x v3 is covered here by
PROJECTING them and requiring their own signatures to still verify: the signature is CC
Corpus's, so a wrong projection fails loudly rather than passing falsely. A genuine served
v3 row is still worth having and is asked for.
Under scripts/, which netlify.toml 404s, so this is not published.

refusals.reason: The attestation verified and its outcome, 'no_procede_reverso_abono', is not one this mandate treats as authorising a payment. Membership in the decider's declared vocabulary is checked elsewhere and is a different question: nothing in verification reads an outcome as permitting anything, so without this a requirement to cite a decision is satisfied by citing a signed DENIAL.

appliedBound.note: The mandate required a decision attestation; the one this payment cited verified, and its outcome is not one this mandate treats as authorising a payment. No spending bound was compared, because no mandate amount constraint was reached.

refusals.reason: This payment moves 2887437 minor units (2 dp) of MXN and the mandate's per_transaction_ceiling is 25000 MXN, which is 2500000 at the same scale. The payment exceeds it and is refused. The constraint breached is `actionScope.per_transaction_ceiling`. This figure is the EFFECTIVE ceiling: a deployment may tighten it below what the credential declares and may never raise it, so compare against the credential to see whether it was tightened.
